title: Rav Bivi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rav Nachman’s student, as in Bava Metzia 23b, where he asked Rav Nachman; in Bava Batra 36b he raised a difficulty against Rav Nachman; in Chagigah 22b and Yevamot 12b he taught before Rav Nachman. In Berakhot 6b, “Rav Bivi said to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak,” Hyman proposes “to Rav Nachman,” or alternatively bar Yaakov.
Likewise we find “Rav Bivi said that Rav Yehudah said,” as in Eruvin 23b.

Hyman describes him as the colleague and groomsman of Rav Yosef, as in Kiddushin 81a: once he visited Rav Yosef’s house; after they had eaten bread, he said, “Remove the ladder from under Bivi,” for Rav Bivi was his groomsman. In Megillah 18b Rav Yosef said, “Hold Rav Bivi’s [view] in your hand,” and he disagrees there with Rav Kahana (Rav’s student) about the words of Rav and Shmuel. In Eruvin 75b: “Rav Yosef said: Rabbi taught … Rav Bivi said to them: Do not listen to him; I said it to him, in the name of Rav Ada bar Ahavah,” etc. In Kiddushin 76b the host of Rav Ada bar Ahavah and Rav Bivi were quarreling over some appointment in the town; they came before Rav Yosef … Rav Yosef wanted to disqualify the host of Rav Ada bar Ahavah because he was a convert, but through Rav Ada bar Ahavah Rav Yosef ruled and said: “Rav Bivi, who is a great man, should attend to matters of Heaven,” etc.

In Shabbat 80b we find that he had a daughter: he coated her limb by limb and took four hundred zuz for her … “Rav Nachman said: Rav Bivi, who drinks beer — his daughters need coating.” Hyman regards Rav Papa as like his student, as in Niddah 27a: Rav Papa sat behind Rav Bivi before Rav Hamnuna (a student-colleague of Rav Chisda) … they laughed at him … “Rav Papa said: Even such a thing a person should say and not keep silent before his teacher.” (Hyman distinguishes him from the Rabbi Bivi mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud, Rabbi Yochanan’s student, who is also called in the Babylonian Talmud Rav Bivi without further designation.) And Yitzchak the Exilarch was the son of Rav Bivi’s sister, as in Yevamot 115b.

notes.text: Saved Kiddushin76b shows RavAda’s host and Bivi himself disputing the appointment, not two hosts. The host’s convert status and Ada’s intervention remain. Hyman’s groomsman relation, generations and distinction from the Palestinian Bivi remain his claims. ר״ג is read Nachman in BavaBatra; the lime-coating account is abridged as before.

The consulted Kiddushin 76b has Rav Ada’s host, a convert, disputing with Bivi himself; Ada’s intervention leads to the distinction between heavenly and town affairs. There are not two disputing hosts. Hyman’s groomsman relation, generation placement, Palestinian Bivi distinction and nephew identification remain his claims; the lime-coating story remains abridged.
